prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give accurate, up-to-date names and phone numbers I’ll need either your Denver ZIP/neighborhood (so I can narrow to nearby practices) or permission to look one up for you. Without live web access I can’t guarantee any specific practice info is current, but I can immediately tell you exactly which types of practices to call, why each is useful, what to ask, and how to pick the best one. That often gets you to the right clinic faster than random searching.

Quick questions
- Which neighborhood or ZIP code in Denver are you in or willing to travel from?
- Do you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon or periodontist) or would you consider a general dentist who does implants?
- Any special needs: IV sedation, same‑day teeth (All‑on‑4), extensive bone grafting, or a strict budget?

If you want a shortlist, tell me your ZIP/neighborhood and I’ll prepare 4–6 nearby practices (oral surgeons, periodontists, and an implant-focused restorative practice), with reasons to call each.

If you want to proceed now, here’s what to do and who to call

1) Which offices to call (and why)
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMS)
  - Why: OMS are surgeons who handle complex implant cases, extractions, bone grafts/sinus lifts and IV/general sedation. Call if you expect bone grafting, multiple implants, impacted teeth, or want sedation.
- Periodontists
  - Why: Specialists in gums and implant placement — good for single implants, bone grafting, soft‑tissue esthetics and long‑term implant health.
- Prosthodontists or implant restorative dentists
  - Why: Prosthodontists focus on the crown/bridge/overdentures that go on implants — call them if you want excellent esthetic/functional restorations or full‑mouth rehab.
- Multi‑specialty implant centers
  - Why: These combine surgeons and restorative specialists in one office for same‑day planning, digital workflow (CBCT + guided surgery), and coordinated care — useful for full arch or complex restorative cases.
- Experienced general dentists with a strong implant referral network
  - Why: For single implants in straightforward situations they may be more convenient and cost‑effective; ensure they work closely with a specialist for complicated steps.

2) Top questions to ask on the phone (or at a consultation)
- Are you a board‑certified oral surgeon/periodontist/prosthodontist? How many years have you placed implants?
- How many implants do you place per year? (Experience matters.)
- Do you use CBCT 3D imaging for planning? Do you do guided/digital implant placement?
- Which implant brands do you use? (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, Dentsply Sirona, etc. — reputable brands matter.)
- Do you perform bone grafts and sinus lifts in‑house? If so, how often?
- What sedation options do you offer (local only, oral sedation, IV sedation, general anesthesia)?
- Will the restorative crown/bridge be done here or by my general dentist? Do you coordinate with a prosthodontist?
- Can I see before/after photos of similar cases and patient references?
- What is the estimated timeline from placement to final crown? What is the price range and what’s included (surgery, imaging, abutment, crown, follow‑ups)?
- Do you offer warranties or guarantees on the implant/restoration? What are payment/financing options?
- What happens if there’s a complication after hours?

3) Red flags to avoid
- Provider won’t allow you to see before/after photos or patient reviews.
- No 3D imaging (CBCT) available for planning complex cases.
- Pushy sales tactics or pressure to do “same‑day teeth” without proper planning.
- Unclear who will do the restorative crown (you want a clear restorative plan).
- Extremely low prices that seem too good to be true — may use inferior components or cut corners.

4) What to expect on cost and timeline (ballpark)
- Single implant + abutment + crown: typically $3,000–$6,000 in Denver (varies widely).
- Bone grafting or sinus lift adds $500–$2,500+ depending on complexity.
- Full-arch solutions (All‑on‑4/All‑on‑X): often $20,000–$40,000+ per arch.
- Healing time before final crown: generally 3–6 months (can be shorter with immediate-load protocols if you’re a candidate).

5) How I’d choose among calls
- Give highest weight to specialists with:
  - Board certification or specialty credentials
  - Regular use of CBCT/digital planning and clear restorative workflow
  - Good before/after portfolio and patient reviews
  - Clear pricing breakdown and follow‑up care plan
  - Proximity and availability for emergencies

If you want a concrete short list
Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer an oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist, or a center that does everything. I’ll draft a 4–6 practice shortlist with why to call each one and a short script you can use when you call.
